newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee called to open little changed.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee called to open little changed.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures were called to open little changed on Wednesday, although some traders expected the market to move higher on the heels of three consecutive sessions of losses.

New York arabica futures ended sharply lower on Tuesday, in a continued technical correction to last week's steep run-up. July settled 6.00 cents per lb lower, at 240.25 cents, after ranging from 245.00 and 239.00 cents. Second-position September fell 5.30 cents to 214.70 cents, while the outer months finished down 0.95 to 6.00.

Technically, traders pegged initial July resistance at 242.00 cents, followed by Tuesday's high of 245.00 cents. Near-term July support was seen at 239.00-238.00 cents, with a breach of that level leading to a test of 232.00 cents.

After Tuesday's close, the CSCE reported certified coffee stocks continued to climb. Stocks increased by 1,770 bags, to 48,962 bags as of May 19. There were 4,000 bags of coffee pending grading, the exchange said.

Focus today is likely to be in London, where a full session of the Association of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC) is meeting to discuss their policy on export quotas in view of the recent explosive futures rally.
At a preparatory session of the ACPC six-member technical group on Monday, delegates said a draft proposal recommended the group retain export quotas but include new flexibility on allocating them.
Ivory Coast Commodity Minister Guy- Alain Gauze said at London coffee talks on Wednesday that he favored retaining a system of export quotas for the six months from July to December.
London July robusta futures slumped early Wednesday, in light trading. LIFFE July was down $38 at the midday break, to $2,037.
